lane: D2 — feasibility of graded opportunities from 97_opportunity_scan
scope_note: Task named 'the five graded opportunities'; 97_/findings.json contains ELEVEN items whose effect is 'raises novelty' (L5-01, L5-02, L5-15) or 'closes an objection' (L5-03,04,05,06,07,08,10,12). All eleven were assessed. L5-09/11/16/17 ('only adds description') and L5-13/14 ('not applicable') were out of scope and not assessed.
method: Existence + size/row-count checks on every named input; motif and region class sizes recomputed only where they decide feasibility (genomic motif-instance counts from ref.fa, canonical per-timepoint motif assignment via 90_/canonical_sites.py, REFA06 dominant-strand class sizes, rebuilt gene-set sizes for L5-10). No item's analysis was run.

findings.location: 97_opportunity_scan/findings.json L5-01 (raises novelty); R1 EN L51 "AAGCCCG 6mA occupancy was likewise stable"
findings.issue: Sole blocker (missing AAGCCCG genomic-instance null core fraction) is now removed: it is computable in seconds from ref.fa with the canonical matcher, and the analysis is runnable end to end. But the null lands at 0.6972, close to the observed T2/T3 values, so the claim it would support ('core-concentrated at every timepoint') is at risk for T2 and T3.
findings.evidence: ref.fa (/Users/okaban/bioinfo/methyl/260102_M145/data/ref.fa, 8,667,507 bp): 1,334 AAGCCCG instances (649 + strand / 685 - strand; matches canon 1,334); 930 of 1,334 fall in core 1.5-7.17 Mb -> null core fraction 0.6972. Observed (90_/tables/aagcccg_pooled_core_fraction_canonical.tsv) 0.8217 / 0.7035 / 0.7296. GCCGGC control reproduces exactly: 16,059 matches -> 32,118 C positions, core fraction 0.6310 = the 0.6309 null in 90_/tables/core_arm_fraction_permutation.tsv.
findings.n: n = 1,334 instances for the null; 1,116 / 1,302 / 1,017 pooled canonical site rows per timepoint (90_ table, reproduced by canonical_sites.aagcccg_pooled_by_timepoint)
findings.provenance: No dependence on 66_ or on the 2026-02 reports. Inputs are 90_ (Sep-21, scripts present) + 01_integration canonical file + ref.fa.
findings.proposed_fix: Runnable as specified. Report the null as 0.6972 (930/1,334) and expect T2/T3 to be only ~0.6-3.3 pp above it: the honest statement is likely 'strongly core-enriched at T1, at-or-near expectation at T2/T3', not 'core-concentrated at every timepoint'. Note the unit: the null is per-instance, so it is 0.6972 whether the denominator is C4 sites, A0/A1 sites or pooled.

findings.location: 97_/findings.json L5-02 (raises novelty); R2 EN L62-64, R6 EN L116
findings.issue: The three contingency tests are runnable from canonical files, but every number in the item must be rebuilt: the unattributed T1 set is 1,516 sites under the canonical matcher, not the 1,674 quoted from 66_.
findings.evidence: canonical_sites.load_canonical() on 01_integration/high_confidence_sites_weighted.csv reproduces canon exactly (GCCGGC 4mC 1,289/1,595/1,073; AAGCCCG 6mA 418/451/443; AAGCCCG 4mC 698/851/574). 6mA totals 1,934/2,120/2,295 (T1 1,934 matches 66_/tables/B4_summary.tsv 6mA_total_T1 1934). Non-AAGCCCG 6mA = 1,516/1,669/1,852. GATC subtraction is a no-op: 0 of the HC 6mA sites sit in a GATC context at any timepoint (43,535 genomic GATC occurrences), so 'minus GATC' changes nothing.

findings.provenance: DEPENDS ON A STALE TABLE: 66_/tables/B4_*.tsv (Sep-11, one script) carries the pre-fix AAGCCCG T1 count 260 vs canonical 418, hence the inflated 1,674. Re-derive the unattributed set with canonical_sites.motif() before quoting any of 64.2% / 88.6% / 2.93% / 1.49% / p = 1.1e-149 / p = 1.7e-5 — none of those were re-verified here.
findings.proposed_fix: Rebuild from the canonical file (one pass, minutes); the 'expected 88.61% proximal' definition must be written out (TSS set and window), since 66_ records no definition. TSS set available: Jeong2016 n = 3,570 (used by 90_/tables/protection_zone_ratio_by_timepoint.tsv).

findings.verdict: FEASIBLE (wider than the item claims) — but the expected null is unlikely to hold
findings.location: 97_/findings.json L5-03 (closes an objection); Discussion EN L252 "GCCGGC 4mC Exhibits Strand-Specific"
findings.issue: Inputs and class sizes are ample, and the file covers more than the item states (8 libraries across all three timepoints, not T1 replicates only). Gene coordinates+strand, absent from 11_epigenome_integration, are available from featureCounts. However a first look at the class sizes shows a strong dominant-strand x gene-strand association, so the test will probably NOT return the independence result the item assumes.
findings.evidence: 91_/tables/REFA06_GCCGGC_per_instance_strand_pct.tsv.gz: 105,339 rows, columns start/plus_pct/minus_pct/sample; samples 1-1,1-2,1-3,2-1,2-3,3-2,3-3,3-4 (8, not 3; 2-2/2-4 absent); 15,666 distinct instances; 95,615 rows have max(plus,minus) = 0. Informative rows (dominant strand >=50%, excluding the 111 both-strand>=50 rows): 8,227 total = 1-1 329 / 1-2 1,057 / 1-3 1,470 / 2-1 1,528 / 2-3 1,462 / 3-2 169 / 3-3 1,286 / 3-4 926. oriC split (<4.27 Mb vs >=): near-balanced in every library, e.g. 1-3 left 386+/360-, right 395+/329-. Gene assignment via 03_quantification/data/featureCounts/featureCounts_M145_s2.txt (8,274 genes with +/- strand): for library 1-3, 1,408 of 1,470 informative instances lie inside a gene, and dominant strand x gene strand is 521/200 (gene +) vs 226/461 (gene -).
findings.n: pooled 8,227 instance-library observations; per-library 169-1,528; 1,408/1,470 inside a gene (library 1-3)
findings.provenance: No dependence on 66_ or on the 2026-02 reports. 91_ is Sep-21 with scripts present. Library 1-1 is PARTIAL: its rows span 6,100-2,998,595 bp only (no oriC-right rows at all), so it cannot enter the oriC-side test; 3-2 contributes only 169 informative instances.
findings.proposed_fix: Runnable. Two cautions before interpretation: (i) exclude 1-1 from the oriC-side test and state the 111 both-strand rows as excluded; (ii) the gene-strand contingency above is provisional (one library, no test run) and could be a coordinate-convention artefact of how 'start' maps to the modified C on each strand — that has to be ruled out first, because if it is real the Discussion gains a transcription-oriented result rather than the clean 'not replication-coupled' negative the item anticipates.

findings.verdict: FEASIBLE (quoting only) — with an unfixable provenance gap

findings.location: 97_/findings.json L5-07 (closes an objection); Supp Fig 7 / Discussion EN L211 region
findings.issue: Region intervals and a canonical-file-based producing script both exist, so the intersection is runnable; what is missing is the motif filter and the statistical test, which are in no script in the repo. Weak because per-region counts are small.
findings.evidence: 72_antismash_genomewide/bgc_summary.tsv: 29 regions with start/end (e.g. region1 86,693-139,654). 72_/scripts/bgc_methylation_proximity.py reads the CANONICAL high_confidence_sites_weighted.csv (L17) and computes internal/flank counts and densities per mod x timepoint - but it applies NO motif filter (mod_type only, L54) and contains no binomial/Fisher test. Canonical GCCGGC-in-BGC totals already recorded: 90_/README.md L29 '140 / 214 / 118 (dedup 140 / 80 / 4 - reproduces the manuscript exactly)'.
findings.n: 29 regions; 140/214/118 canonical GCCGGC 4mC sites in-region across the whole BGC set (i.e. ~5/7/4 per region on average)
findings.provenance: 72_ output is canonical-file-derived (not 66_, not 2026-02). The manuscript's 140/80/4 is first-appearance-derived, per the 90_ audit. The over/under-targeting test behind Supp Fig 7 has no producing script anywhere - it must be written, not re-run.

findings.verdict: FEASIBLE (after mandatory rebuild) — and the rebuild makes it stronger, not weaker
findings.location: 97_/findings.json L5-10 (closes an objection); Discussion EN L234-245
findings.issue: Every quoted correlation depends on tables built from the first-appearance motif assignments, so all of them must be discarded and recomputed. The rebuild is runnable and would have roughly five times the n the item assumes, which changes the item from an underpowered null into a usable bound.
findings.evidence: 28_MTase_stability/run_analysis.py and run_analysis_v2.py read 23_/4mC_motif_assignment.csv and 6mA_motif_assignment.csv (first-appearance tables; on the do-not-use list for per-timepoint counts). The damage is visible in the output: 28_/tables/motif_site_dynamics.tsv gives AAGCCCG T2_vs_T1 gained 64 / lost 260 / stable 0 / loss_fraction 1.0 - a mathematically impossible stability for a methylome with Jaccard 0.700. Rebuilt gene sets from canonical AAGCCCG 6mA sites (418/451/443) intersected with featureCounts gene bodies: 325/341/327 genes per timepoint; 277 (T1&T2), 269 (T1&T3), 280 (T2&T3) carry a site at both timepoints of a contrast; 264 of the 277 have a DESeq2 log2FC in integrated_methyl_expression_weighted.csv (8,083 genes, 7,496 with padj_T2_vs_T1). Detectable |rho| at 80% power: 0.373 at n = 54 (current), 0.172 at n = 264.
findings.n: rebuilt n approx. 264-280 per contrast (vs 45-59 in the existing table); CCGG family rows already 269-307
findings.provenance: DEPENDS ON STALE TABLES: all four 28_ tables are Feb-24 2026 and first-appearance-derived. Not 66_-derived, but equally unusable. The scan's quoted -0.127 (p 0.36, n 54) / -0.049 / -0.149 and the CCGG 0.031-0.088 must not be quoted before the rebuild. The p = 0.016 unattributed row (n = 397) is also stale and, after rebuild, needs multiplicity handling across the 15 rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-point run_analysis_v2.py at 01_integration/high_confidence_sites_weighted.csv via canonical_sites.motif(), rerun, and state the null with the rebuilt n and the detectable-|rho| bound (approx. 0.17 at n = 264). Keep it gene-level and say so; a site-level version would need the per-site occupancy series, which is what the stale table was.
